units.notes:
## Starter vocabulary

| Votic | English |
| --- | --- |
| tere | hi / hello |
| miä õõn | I am |

> These starter examples are provided for demonstration and should be checked by a Votic speaker before being used as authoritative language instruction. ## Votic basics

Votic uses the Latin alphabet with additional **accents**. ##Vocabulary 

| Votic | English |
| --- | --- |
| tere | hi |
| miä õõn | I am |
| siä õõd | you are | 
 | -ko | questions marker | 
 | üvva omnikkoa | good morning | 
 | üvva päivää | good afternoon | 
 | üvva ohtõgoa | good night | 


 ##Verb conjugation 
As you can see from the words for _I am_, and _you are_, we use the stem õõ to mean to be. The infinitive (simplest form) of the verb is actually õlla, however verb stems often differ greatly from their infinitive in Votic. You might also have noticed, that the endings on õõ- change depending on who is doing the action. For miä(I), this is '-n', and for 'siä'(you), this is '-d'.
